rationale: The collective fasting and entreaty before assembling for war resemble the Mizpah preparations with prayer and fasting; the three-day observance here is not the one-day fast specified there.

Both accounts introduce the accession of Demetrius son of Seleucus after a sea arrival; this account names Tripolis and a strong force and fleet, whereas the companion account mentions departure from Rome and arrival with a few men.
